findings.desc: boundValidationEvidenceOutput (packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:239-315) only elides/pops entries from result.commands. It never touches result.details, but executeValidationPlan (same file, ~line 845-850) pushes each already-trimmed commands[i].output into details a SECOND time, line-by-line: `details.push(...result.output.trim().split(\n).filter(Boolean).map((line) => `  ${line}`))`. So details duplicates the same content the bounding tiers elide, and that duplicate is spread verbatim through `...source` in the internal render() closure (line 267) with no reduction. Reproduced against the built dist (packages/main/dist/core/validation-executor.js) with a ValidationResult shaped exactly like executeValidationPlan produces (commands + a details array built by the same duplication the production code performs, not the empty details:[] the smoke test hardcodes): at 2800 commands x 12,000-char output (the real per-command trimOutput cap), details alone serializes to 33,772,491 bytes -- already past both VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES (25,165,824 = 24 MiB) and VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_READ_CEILING_BYTES (33,554,432 = 32 MiB). Calling boundValidationEvidenceOutput on that object elides all 2800 command outputs (elidedCommandOutputs=2800) and then pops every single command entry (elidedCommandEntries=2800, commands.length reaches 0), yet the returned artifact still serializes to 33,772,843 bytes -- OVER the ceiling -- while the function reports bounded:true and state:"bounded", and formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory renders "It reached the 24.00 MiB bound, so it was serialised at 32.21 MiB" as if bounding succeeded. This directly falsifies the invariant asserted in the module doc comment (validation-executor.ts, the paragraph immediately above VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_READ_CEILING_BYTES): "a bounded artifact is always readable by the read whose ceiling bounds it, because VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES is strictly below VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_READ_CEILING_BYTES." That inequality is true only of the two constants; it is not enforced by the code once result.details independently exceeds the bound, because the bounding logic has no lever on details at all. It is exactly the concept-review target pattern: an absolute guarantee ("always readable... by construction") that holds on the tested path and is false on the real production path. validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts never catches this because every fixture it builds via its local validationResult() helper hardcodes details: [] (see smoke lines ~44-53), so the ONE realistic object shape that would exercise this -- the details array executeValidationPlan actually produces, which duplicates the same growth driver CHK-004 targeted (the NUMBER of configured validate commands) -- is never constructed by the tests. Practically: this repository grew validate.commands from 56 to 100 in a single day per the story context (B-9ff1); the details duplication scales with the identical driver, so reaching the few-thousand-command regime where this manifests is the same kind of unbounded growth this story exists to end, and when it is reached the artifact can again exceed the metadata read ceiling and reproduce the original ENOBUFS/"verified metadata changed" failure -- silently, because evidenceBound.bounded=true is reported. Suggested fix direction (not prescribing implementation): either fold details into the same byte budget (e.g. drop/replace details once the bound is not achievable by commands elision alone, and report that in evidenceBound), or derive/replace details from the already-bounded commands array rather than serializing it as an independent duplicate.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29968050ff / 2365be5586. The cross-vendor reviewer's framing was adopted over my own: the requirement was not to also bound details but to enforce a postcondition, because whack-a-mole on fields cannot terminate. Reproduced first - details alone serialised to 35,158,761 bytes, over both bound and ceiling - then rebuilt as staged reduction: command output, the details duplicate, warnings, command entries, then unknown top-level fields NAMED as they are dropped, ending in a measured check plus a verdict-only record whose size cannot depend on the input because every value is a short or truncated scalar. bounded:true is now a property of the measured result rather than of having run the loops. At the reviewer's own scales: 2100 commands 25253823 became 985312; 2800 commands 33672023 became 1314312; details-only 35158761 became 576220; bulk hidden in an unknown field 31457531 became 305. The doc comment no longer asserts an absolute - it separates what is enforced, the returned string being under the bound by measurement, from what is not, since the file also carries verificationCoverage, commandExecution and routineValidationIdentity written outside this string. That residue is precisely why F-003's diagnostic path had to be correct.

findings.desc: CHK-003:adversarial:0 binds an un-falsifiable RED-before-GREEN claim to the wrong selector. The intent requires demonstrating 'the regression test fails when run without the maxBuffer fix (demonstrated by running against the pre-fix tree or by temporarily reverting the maxBuffer additions)'. Its bound selector, 'a genuine post-verification change still reports verified metadata changed' (red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs section 8, line 339), tests something unrelated: that a REAL digest mismatch is still correctly reported post-fix. That section never runs on the pre-fix tree and never reverts the fix, so it proves nothing about RED-before-GREEN. No other bound selector in the 24-intent set covers this claim either. The only committed artefact bearing on it is .lattice/story/actives/B-3434/red-evidence.json, whose failingCommand points at an ephemeral, uncommitted scratch script (a scratchpad path under a session tmpdir), not at the committed test file -- so within the story's own evidence chain, RED-before-GREEN for the actual committed regression is only ASSERTED (commit message prose + that indirect record), never mechanically verified. I independently checked out the RED commit ec18da8da6 (before fix commit 8250774c9d) into an isolated clone, built packages/main from that pre-fix source (confirmed zero maxBuffer occurrences), and ran the actual committed red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs against it: 6 of 8 sections genuinely FAIL, reproducing verified metadata changed after manifest verification verbatim. So the underlying claim is TRUE, but the story shipped no mechanical selector or artefact that proves it -- exactly the pass-for-the-wrong-reason pattern this lane exists to catch. Recommend re-binding CHK-003:adversarial:0 to a fixture-comparison test (e.g. a committed script that asserts failure against a checked-out pre-fix ref, or at minimum wiring the selector to something that actually differs between the two trees) rather than to an unrelated section.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29968050ff / 2365be5586. Two reviewers had independently rebuilt the pre-fix tree and confirmed six of eight sections fail there, so the claim was true - but it was not checkable from the story's own artefacts, which is what the finding was about. The regression now carries the pre-fix helper verbatim, without maxBuffer and with the bare catch, and asserts opposite outcomes on one fixture, plus a below-ceiling control proving size is the only variable. RED-before-GREEN is now provable from committed artefacts alone, with no rebuild of an old tree and no ephemeral scratch script.

findings.desc:
Reproduced: a blob that exceeds METADATA_BLOB_READ_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES (32 MiB) does NOT fail with a clean diagnostic. It reproduces the original silent-content-loss defect in a new, arguably worse form: the "unreadable" error string is populated with up to ~32 MiB of the blob's own raw partial content, not a diagnostic message.

Root cause: describeChildProcessFailure (core/done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts:607-618) does `[err.stderr, err.stdout].map(String).filter(Boolean)` and takes the first non-empty candidate as "detail". This is correct for hook-style catches where stdout/stderr carry short human messages, but isolatedBlobHash/treeBlobHash (lines 641, 661) call `git show` specifically to read blob CONTENT on stdout. On ENOBUFS, Node kills the child but still populates err.stdout with whatever partial content was buffered before the limit hit (confirmed empirically: a 2,000,000-byte write against maxBuffer:1,048,576 produced err.stdout.length === 1,056,768, a non-empty Buffer, while err.stderr was an empty-but-truthy Buffer). describeChildProcessFailure's filter drops the empty stderr and selects the huge stdout buffer as "the diagnostic", string-ifying up to the full maxBuffer worth of blob bytes into the returned `error` field.

Direct repro against the current built dist (packages/main/dist/core/done-prepare-generated-metadata.js), no source changes:
  - staged a 40 MiB deterministic blob ('A' x 40*1024*1024) in a scratch git repo
  - called the exported `isolatedBlobHash(root, indexFile, 'big.bin')`
  - result: `{ ok:false, kind:'unreadable', error: "ENOBUFS: AAAA...AAAA" }` with `error.length === 33,562,633` (~32 MiB), i.e. the "diagnostic" IS the raw blob content, not a description of the failure.

Propagation: this `error` string is not truncated anywhere downstream. verifyMetadataBlobDigests (line 701) folds it into `result.reason` for commitImmutableMetadataTree; commitDonePrepareGeneratedMetadata (line ~1041) re-wraps it as `isolated generated metadata commit failed: ${committed.reason}`; handlers/done-prepare.ts:2364-2367 puts it, unbounded, into `setStep(..., 'blocked', autoCommit.reason)` and into the `reason` field of the `blocked({...})` payload, whose `block()` function (handlers/done-prepare.ts:599-615) builds the literal CLI text output via `reason: ${args.reason}`. A ~32 MiB blob dump therefore becomes the done_prepare CLI's printed/returned output — i.e. an unbounded artifact reproducing exactly the class of defect (oversized undiagnosed content blocking a phase transition) that this story exists to eliminate, just relocated to the CLI-output/step-reason surface instead of test-evidence.json.

This is a live, not merely theoretical, risk: commitImmutableMetadataTree/isolatedBlobHash/treeBlobHash are shared by ALL THREE files this module manages (SAFE_GENERATED_METADATA_FILENAMES at line 131: done-required-evidence.json, process-events.jsonl, test-evidence.json), and only test-evidence.json got an aggregate bound in this story (CHK-004/005, validation-executor.ts). process-events.jsonl is an append-only, never-truncated log across a story's entire lifecycle with no size bound at all; a real story in this same worktree set already carries one at 507,753 bytes (/Users/jek/Documents/Work/proofbound/.worktrees/B-d0b8/.lattice/story/actives/B-235e/process-events.jsonl), and this repository's culture of multi-round adversarial marathons (9+ review rounds observed elsewhere) makes continued organic growth toward the 32 MiB ceiling plausible over a story's life, not far-fetched.

The task's central question for this lane was: "does the new code fail with a diagnostic, or reproduce the original silent-null defect at a higher number?" The answer, verified by direct execution against the built dist, is neither exactly — it fails LOUD but with an undiagnosable, multi-megabyte payload standing in for the diagnostic, at exactly the boundary (>32 MiB) the ceiling was supposed to make safe. No committed test (RED or smoke) exercises a blob above METADATA_BLOB_READ_MAX_BUFFER_BYTES; the RED test's adversarial checks stop at confirming the maxBuffer literal is present and >= 10 MiB, never at driving a read past it.

Suggested remediation direction (not prescriptive): describeChildProcessFailure should not treat "non-empty stdout/stderr buffer" as inherently diagnostic — for ENOBUFS specifically (already distinguished via err.code) it should synthesize a bounded message (e.g. "content exceeds the N-byte read ceiling") rather than stringify captured stdout/stderr, since for a content-bearing read that captured content is truncated garbage, not a diagnostic, by construction.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29968050ff / 2365be5586, and this was the most serious finding of the round because it was this story reproducing its own defect one order of magnitude up. Above the ceiling the returned error WAS the partial blob: reproduced live on the pre-fix build at 31,800,592 characters beginning with the blob bytes. Root cause confirmed at source: describeChildProcessFailure took the first non-empty of stderr then stdout, and git show puts CONTENT on stdout, so an ENOBUFS that leaves stderr empty made the partial capture the diagnostic. Repaired by splitting into two describers chosen by which stream actually carries meaning - describeContentReadFailure reads stderr only and synthesises a diagnostic naming the ceiling and the captured byte count, describeDiagnosticStreamFailure keeps stdout because a hook's diagnostic genuinely lives there - with MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_CHARS on both as the general defence, since ENOBUFS was only the instance found. Measured after: 31800592 characters became 118. The blast radius is asserted end to end: the commitImmutableMetadataTree reason that becomes done_prepare's printed block text is 231 characters, names the ceiling, and is asserted to contain no non-ASCII so a content leak fails loudly. The regression fixture is process-events.jsonl deliberately, because it is append-only, never truncated, and is the managed file that will actually arrive at the ceiling. Independently reproduced by the cross-vendor reviewer at the exact ceiling and by me.

findings.desc: Of the 24 bound selectors, two embed a numeric count despite the stated policy that pinned selectors must carry no count (per the identical boilerplate note on every verificationEvidence entry, and the B-9ff1 history of stranded count-bearing selectors). CHK-001:happy:0's 'commitImmutableMetadataTree commits a 1,400,000-byte staged blob' is safe: 1,400,000 is a literal baked directly into the section() title string in red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs (line 144), chosen once by the author and immune to drift from unrelated code changes -- it can only change if someone edits that literal string itself. CHK-005:edge:0's 'artifact (1212174 bytes) is unbounded and silent' is NOT safe by the same reasoning: 1212174 is validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts line 131's runtime-computed bounded.measuredBytes (JSON.stringify of a synthetic 100-command fixture), interpolated into the console.log via template literal. Any future change to the shape of commandResult/validationResult (e.g. adding a field for closer fidelity to the real evidence.json shape, or changing trimOutput's 12,000-char cap) will silently shift this byte count and break the pinned selector -- reproducing exactly the B-9ff1 failure mode this policy exists to prevent. Notably the same file demonstrates awareness of this exact risk two sections later: line 212's marker/JSON-contract selector and line 239's entry-cap selector both deliberately pick number-free tails ('JSON contract intact', 'a diagnostic count') specifically to dodge adjacent printed byte counts ('30036374-byte artifact bounded to 25143521 bytes, 49 marker(s)'), but that same discipline was not applied to line 131's '(1212174 bytes)' text. Recommend re-binding CHK-005:edge:0 to a number-free substring of the same output line, e.g. 'is unbounded and silent'.
findings.resolvedReason: The unsafe pin could not be repaired and is permanently waived with full reasoning; the safe one was left alone as intended. CHK-005:edge:0 was pinned to (1212174 bytes), a runtime measurement of a fixture that did not model details. F-001's repair made that fixture model the producer correctly, so the same shape now measures 2487463 bytes. The number changed because the fixture became more truthful, not because behaviour regressed. Printing the old literal would publish a number the code no longer produces, and wiping the pin to re-pin it would defeat the mechanism that exists to prevent exactly that, so both escapes were refused. Every other section line is now a count-free sentence with measured numbers moved to an indented line beneath, so no future selector can bind to a runtime measurement. CHK-001:happy:0's 1,400,000-byte literal is untouched because it is a literal in the section title and cannot drift. A second class emerged during the repair and is worth separating: a count-free sentence is still editable prose, so the reworded section broke CHK-004:adversarial:1 without any number being involved; that phrase was restored verbatim and marked load-bearing in a comment naming its pin.

findings.desc:
describeChildProcessFailure was introduced by this fix specifically to avoid the "empty-but-truthy stderr Buffer" pitfall (its own doc comment names this exact bug), but it is not applied at 4 other catch sites in the same file that construct diagnostics from the same execFileSync error shape with the pre-existing naive pattern `String(err?.stderr || err?.stdout || err?.message || err).trim()`:
  - gitMaybe, line 376
  - rollbackDonePrepareGeneratedMetadataTransaction, line 494
  - runCommitHook, line 759
  - commitImmutableMetadataTree's index-refresh-failure catch, line 955, and its outer catch, line 965

Currently these specific call sites (rev-parse HEAD, symbolic-ref, update-ref, hook path/args, index-info restore) carry low practical risk since their normal output is small, so this is not independently reproducible as a live incident the way F-003 is. But it is a real inconsistency: the module now states an explicit diagnosability invariant (CHK-002's own goal, "make the surfaced reason name the underlying error so the next person does not spend hours attributing it to concurrency") and built a dedicated helper for it, yet applied that helper to only 2 of the module's ~7 catch sites that wrap execFileSync failures. Any future change that routes larger content through isolatedGit (used for read-tree/add/write-tree/commit-tree, all under the outer catch at line 965) inherits the same empty-buffer-selection defect the new helper was written to fix.

Recommend either applying describeChildProcessFailure uniformly at all execFileSync catch sites in this file, or documenting why these five are exempt.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29968050ff / 2365be5586, and the implementer caught a real regression of its own in the process. Routing all four remaining catch sites through the new describers broke done-prepare-auto-closeout-smoke, which asserts a specific hook-failure wording. That file is outside allowedModify, and adjusting an assertion to fit new wording would have been the wrong repair regardless. Fixed on the merits instead: a hook that failed has already explained itself, so the diagnostic-stream describer prefixes only a Node-level code and never a plain exit status, while the content-read describer keeps exit 128 because there stderr is often all there is. done-prepare-auto-closeout-smoke, quorum-submit-smoke and validation-evidence-reuse-smoke all pass.

findings.desc: CHK-004:happy:0, CHK-004:edge:1 and CHK-004:adversarial:0 are all bound to the same selector, 'JSON contract intact' (validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts line 212), which does not evidence any of the three claims. happy:0 requires 'exactly one of two shipped outcomes exists' (A: code bound in the real serialization path, or B: a committed rationale doc) -- a governance/disposition judgment about production wiring that a pure-function unit test cannot establish; the smoke test only exercises boundValidationEvidenceOutput/formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory in isolation and never checks they are actually invoked by the real evidence-write path in handlers/verifier.ts. I independently confirmed by reading verifier.ts lines 842-851 that boundValidationEvidenceOutput and formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory ARE genuinely wired into the evidence object written to test-evidence.json, so outcome A is truly shipped today -- but nothing in CHK-004's mechanical evidence chain proves this, and a future refactor that silently un-wires those two calls (while leaving the standalone smoke test untouched) would sail through every CHK-004 selector unnoticed. edge:1 describes outcome B (rationale-doc path), which does not even apply since outcome A was chosen -- binding it to a code-behavior selector makes it vacuously/irrelevantly satisfied regardless of whether any rationale document exists. adversarial:0 requires proving the item was NOT closed with 'only a prose paragraph... with no shipped consequence' -- again not something a JSON.parse-succeeds assertion can demonstrate. Only CHK-004:edge:0 (bound to the same section, which does assert visible truncation markers, elidedCommandOutputs>0, and no silent data loss) is a direct, specific match for its own claim. Recommend re-binding happy:0/edge:1/adversarial:0 to a check that greps or imports handlers/verifier.ts to confirm boundValidationEvidenceOutput is actually called in the persisted-evidence path, rather than reusing the standalone smoke test's generic pass line.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29968050ff / 2365be5586. The three CHK-004 intents are governance claims about which of two outcomes shipped, and were bound to a serialization check that could never observe the disposition. A new section now reads handlers/verifier.ts and asserts the disposition itself: that boundValidationEvidenceOutput and formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory are called inside persistStoryValidationEvidence, that the record serialises the bounded output, that the plain JSON.stringify is gone rather than shadowed, and that the outcome-B rationale document does not exist. A future silent un-wiring now fails a test instead of passing unnoticed.

findings.desc: Three lower-severity assertion-strength gaps, all convenience bindings rather than incorrect ones (the underlying behavior is genuinely correct on manual source inspection, but the bound selector under-proves the specific claim). (1) CHK-002:edge:0 claims the surfaced reason 'includes the original error message or code from the child process'; its selector's section only asserts String(unreadable.error).length > 0 (red-b3434-blob-buffer-ceiling.mjs line 278) -- any non-empty placeholder would satisfy this, it does not check the content actually derives from the child process. I confirmed describeChildProcessFailure (done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts lines 607-616) genuinely composes code+stderr/stdout/message, so the feature is correct; the test just doesn't prove it. (2) CHK-002:adversarial:1 claims the unreadable-blob message is 'textually distinct from the error message for a blob that is genuinely absent'; its bound section (line 303) never touches the absent-blob path at all, so no assertion anywhere in the file directly compares the two message strings for inequality -- only the structural kind field ('absent' vs 'unreadable', asserted in the different section bound to CHK-002:edge:0/adversarial:0) is checked. (3) CHK-005:adversarial:0 ('the advisory never changes the pass/fail verdict') is bound to 'validation-evidence-buffer-smoke: PASS' -- the whole-file summary banner, the least specific selector possible, printed identically regardless of which of the file's 7 sections is at issue. Sections 4/5 do preserve allPass alongside advisory generation, so the claim holds, but the selector itself carries no discriminating power for this specific claim over any other in the file. None of these three block the story; recommend tightening the assertions/selectors in a follow-up rather than in this story.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 29968050ff / 2365be5586. Absent now asserts exit 128, the fatal marker and the path; unreadable asserts the actual not-a-git-repository text; and the two are cross-compared directly - unequal, neither containing the other, neither carrying the other's vocabulary - which is what the intent claimed and the previous assertion never checked.

Fixed in commit 78465a6d32, and the repair changed the shape rather than patching the vector. The literal bounded flag is gone; the result now carries withinBound, derived from the measured serialized size, alongside reduced which records that a reduction ran. Those are different questions and conflating them was the defect: a flag that structurally cannot report false converts a failure into a false assurance, which is the catch-returns-null shape this story exists to remove, one layer up. Every embedded string is now capped including key names, which was the dimension the earlier staged reduction missed - the third dimension of the same family after values and the details duplicate. Verified by me against the built artefact using the reviewer's own vector, a top-level field whose key name is thirty million characters: before the fix it produced 30,000,284 bytes with the flag reporting true, after the fix it produces 417 bytes. A regression covering bulk in a key name is committed, and the smoke asserts the flag agrees with the measurement, which is the assertion whose absence let a wrong flag pass every fixture.

findings.desc:
Minor wording inaccuracy in formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory: the "bounded" branch renders `Top-level field(s) removed: ${sizing.droppedKeys.join(', ')}` (validation-executor.ts ~L242-244), but droppedKeys is populated by two different stages with different semantics. Stage 5 (L438-446) genuinely deletes the key from `carried`. Stage 6 (L453-457) TRUNCATES a long string field in place (keeps the key, replaces the value with a 1000-char prefix plus a countElisionMarker) and pushes the SAME key onto droppedKeys via `if (!droppedKeys.includes(key)) droppedKeys.push(key)`. So a stage-6 field is reported to the operator as "removed" when it is actually still present in the artifact, truncated.

Verified directly: `boundValidationEvidenceOutput({ status: 'pass', allPass: true, summary: 'S'.repeat(50_000_000) })` returns parsed output with `summary` present (truncated to a 1000-char prefix + marker) while `evidenceBound.droppedKeys` contains "summary" and formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory renders "Top-level field(s) removed: summary."

This is not a silent-loss defect -- the reader who opens the artifact sees the field is present with an inline "...omitted so..." marker stating the truncated char count, so nobody is misled about content actually disappearing. It is purely an advisory-text accuracy issue: "removed" overclaims for the truncation case. Low severity; recommend either renaming the shared array (e.g. `affectedKeys`) or splitting stage-5 deletions from stage-6 truncations so the advisory can say "removed" only for the former and "truncated" for the latter.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 78465a6d32. Fields truncated in place and fields removed outright now report as the different dispositions they are - the smoke section prints droppedKeys and truncatedKeys separately - rather than sharing one array and one label that described only half of them accurately.

findings.desc:
F-003's "231 characters ... done_prepare printed block text" names an intermediate value, not the text a person sees; real block text is larger (no leak found in either binary or ASCII-shaped adversarial fixtures, so the safety property holds -- this is an evidence-precision gap, not a functional defect).

Reproduced the over-ceiling read end to end myself against dist rebuilt from the current HEAD (97d764b885), independently of the RED test, using the real shipped functions (isolatedBlobHash / commitImmutableMetadataTree), with two fixtures: (a) a high-entropy binary blob matching the RED test's own construction, and (b) a purpose-built blob whose bytes are ALL printable ASCII, containing a distinctive canary string ("SECRET_MARKER_CANARY_...") near the start of the file, specifically to defeat the non-ASCII assertion the RED test relies on (a leak of ASCII content would not trip that assertion).

Result: no leak in either case, at any layer. The canary string never appears in isolatedBlobHash's error, in commitImmutableMetadataTree's reason, or in the constructed done_prepare block text. This part of F-003's claim holds, confirmed independently.

What does not hold: the "231 characters" figure describes an intermediate value, not the text a person sees. Tracing the real call chain (done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts:1126, done-prepare.ts:2367, done-prepare.ts:599-604 -- all current line numbers), a failure description is wrapped THREE more times after commitImmutableMetadataTree's reason before a person sees anything:
  1. isolatedBlobHash returns a 118-char error (matches the RED test's own "errorChars=118" instrumentation, reconfirmed on this HEAD).
  2. commitImmutableMetadataTree.reason = "verified metadata could not be read from the isolated index: ... (read ceiling 33554432 bytes)" = 231 chars (matches the RED test's own "commit reason chars: 231" instrumentation; reconfirmed byte-identical on this HEAD on both the binary and ASCII fixtures).
  3. commitDonePrepareGeneratedMetadata prepends "isolated generated metadata commit failed: " (43 chars) -> 274 chars.
  4. done-prepare.ts's blocked() prepends "DONE prepare auto-closeout refused: " (36 chars) -> 310 chars, rendered as "reason: <text>" -> 318 chars for that one line; the minimal 3-line block ("DONE prepare: BLOCKED\nblockedAt: cleanTree\nreason: ...") is 361 chars. The real full CLI output is larger still: block() also emits a "files:" section naming the path and repeats a near-identical reason inside "Steps:" (cleanTree: BLOCKED - <same 310-char text>), plus "next:" and, when the manifest has unsafe entries, a "generated metadata delta" guidance section (done-prepare.ts:550-571) -- all built from short static strings/paths only, so still no content leak, but the printed text is meaningfully larger than 231, not equal to it.

Neither the committed RED test nor F-003's resolvedReason narrative ("the commitImmutableMetadataTree reason that becomes done_prepare's printed block text is 231 characters ... asserted end to end") actually exercises done-prepare.ts's block() rendering or the intermediate commitDonePrepareGeneratedMetadata wrapper. Both stop at commitImmutableMetadataTree's own return value and describe that as reaching the CLI text, which overstates the coverage: nothing committed asserts the true end-user-visible string or its length, and nothing would catch a future change to either wrapping prefix, to buildGeneratedMetadataDirtyGuidance, or to the files:/Steps: rendering silently reintroducing unbounded content at those specific call sites (as distinct from the isolatedBlobHash/treeBlobHash sites, which the ceiling logic does correctly guard end to end, and which is what actually matters for safety -- the F-008/F-009 fix in this same round, for example, was caught precisely because a smoke assertion compared a flag against a fresh measurement; the equivalent comparison does not exist for this wrapping chain).

Net: the safety property (no content leak, bounded diagnostic) is real, and I independently verified it including against an ASCII-shaped adversarial fixture the non-ASCII assertion cannot catch. What is not real is the "231 characters ... end to end" framing and the implied test coverage of the full printed block text. Recommend either correcting the resolvedReason's wording (change "is 231 characters" to name commitImmutableMetadataTree's reason specifically, not the printed block text), or adding one assertion that drives the failure through commitDonePrepareGeneratedMetadata (or the real done-prepare.ts handler) and checks the actual wrapped reason stays small and content-free, so the two remaining un-exercised wrapping layers are covered by something other than a reviewer's ad hoc reproduction.
findings.resolvedReason: Correct, and the imprecision was mine. My F-003 resolution said the reason that becomes done_prepare's printed block text is 231 characters. The 231-character measurement is of the commitImmutableMetadataTree reason - an intermediate value - not of the block text a person actually reads, which wraps that reason in additional framing and is therefore larger. Conflating the two is the same category of error this story spent nine findings removing from the code: a measurement of one thing presented as a measurement of another. The correction is recorded here and the TEST summary states the distinction rather than repeating the conflation. What the reviewer verified, and what actually matters, is that the safety property holds on both fixtures: it reproduced the over-ceiling read end to end against a dist rebuilt from current HEAD, using the real shipped isolatedBlobHash and commitImmutableMetadataTree rather than the RED test's harness, with a high-entropy binary blob and - the case I asked for specifically, because the no-non-ASCII assertion cannot catch a leak of ASCII content - an ASCII-shaped blob. No content leak in either. So the diagnostic is bounded and content-free as claimed; only my sentence about which string was measured was wrong.

findings.desc: validation-executor.ts:139-152 (the 'What is guaranteed, and what is not' block immediately above VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_READ_CEILING_BYTES) states unconditionally: 'GUARANTEED, as an enforced post-condition of boundValidationEvidenceOutput: the string it returns is strictly smaller than VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES. It is enforced by measuring the real encoding after every stage and by a last-resort replacement that cannot fail.' This is false for a reachable input. The early-return branch at line 375 (measuredBytes < VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES || !result || typeof result !== 'object') returns the raw unbounded serialized string with NO stage and NO last-resort replacement (verdictOnlyRecord is only reachable from the object-shaped pipeline) whenever result is a non-object bulk value (e.g. a bare oversized string) whose size is already over the bound; that branch legitimately sets withinBound=false and hands back an over-bound output. This is exactly what the story's own smoke fixture 8e exercises and asserts as honest, not a hypothetical: boundValidationEvidenceOutput(x.repeat(30*MIB)) -> withinBound===false, actualBytes>=BOUND (confirmed live: node packages/main/dist/tasks/validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.js prints 'an unmet bound is reported honestly instead of being flagged as success / measured=31457282 serialised=31457282 withinBound=false'). Git history shows the two pieces of prose were never reconciled: the GUARANTEED paragraph was authored in commit 29968050ff (the F-001 fix round); the branch that can legitimately return withinBound=false on this exact path (previously a hardcoded bounded:false literal, now a genuine measurement per the F-008 fix) was made honest later in commit 78465a6d3, which added an inline comment right at that branch acknowledging the gap ('a non-object carrying bulk...has no structure to reduce, so this path can legitimately return withinBound=false') but did not revisit the module-level GUARANTEED paragraph nine lines above to add the same caveat. The doc's own framing -- 'stated precisely, because an earlier revision of this comment claimed an invariant that the code did not enforce' -- is itself undermined by this residual unconditional claim: it is the same defect family (comment claims an absolute the code enforces only conditionally) recurring in the very paragraph rewritten to correct that family, one field the paragraph never mentions later (measuredBytes 1160). Production is not at risk today: verifier.ts:849 (if (!boundedOutput.withinBound) return persistenceFailure(...)) checks the flag rather than trusting the doc absolute. But a future maintainer who trusts 'GUARANTEED...It is enforced by...a last-resort replacement that cannot fail' as license to skip that check at a new call site would reintroduce exactly the over-trusted-invariant shape F-001/F-008 exist to remove. Suggested fix: qualify the GUARANTEED clause with the same caveat already present at the code site, e.g. state the guarantee conditionally on withinBound (or on result being object-shaped / already under the bound) rather than as an absolute of the function itself.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 353eec69e1, and the repair records the mechanism rather than only correcting the claim. The paragraph asserted an enforced post-condition that the code contradicted nine lines below it, on the early-return branch where a non-object carrying bulk has no structure to reduce and legitimately returns withinBound false. I reproduced it: a 31,457,280-character primitive in, 31,457,282 bytes out, withinBound false, bound 25,165,824. The drift was traced exactly - the GUARANTEED prose was written during the F-001 round, the honest branch was added later during the F-008 fix, and the implementer wrote the caveat immediately beside the code without revisiting the paragraph above it. The new text separates what is guaranteed for an input the reduction can act on from what happens to an input with no structure to reduce, and states plainly that persistStoryValidationEvidence refuses the write rather than storing an artifact the metadata read cannot consume. It also records why the sentence went stale: a sentence about behaviour has to be re-read whenever the behaviour changes, or it becomes the most confident wrong thing in the file. Worth noting for the record that the paragraph's own opening sentence already warned about an earlier revision claiming an invariant the code did not enforce - a comment written specifically to prevent overclaiming became an overclaim, which is why the mechanism and not just the correction is now in the file.

findings.desc: Two residual doc/code gaps in the same function, both in the true last-resort path that the function's own doc comment never describes. (1) validation-executor.ts:341-357's doc for boundValidationEvidenceOutput says 'Nothing is discarded silently' and enumerates stage 1 through stage 5 as the reduction pipeline ('stage 5 - last resort: drop the largest remaining top-level fields, NAMING each one'), then separately states 'The verdict-bearing fields (allPass, allPassed, status, failureKind, summary) are preserved at every stage.' The code has moved past that description: there is a stage 6 (line 503, truncate remaining oversized strings in place) and, beyond even that, the verdictOnlyRecord fallback (line 525) -- neither is named in this doc block, so a reader of it does not know the pipeline has two more tiers. (2) Inside that undocumented final tier, verdictOnlyRecord (line 562) rebuilds the output from only 6 fields (provider, status, allPass, allPassed, failureKind, summary); it silently omits 2 of the 8 fields in the verdictKeys set defined at line 489 (timestamp, headSha) that stage 5 treats as protected/undroppable-by-name specifically so they are never candidates for the named-and-counted droppedKeys mechanism. When verdictOnlyRecord fires, timestamp and headSha vanish from the embedded output string with no entry in droppedKeys or truncatedKeys -- the one case in the whole function where a field disappears without being named, contradicting the 'Nothing is discarded silently' framing for the two fields the code itself classifies as verdict-bearing but the function's own field list (5 named fields, omitting provider/timestamp/headSha from that specific sentence) does not cover. Practical impact is low and confirmed bounded: evaluateValidationEvidenceAdmissibility (validation-evidence-admissibility.ts, outputPassState) only parses allPass/allPassed from the embedded output string, and persistStoryValidationEvidence (verifier.ts) sources the persisted evidence headHash/timestamp independently of boundedOutput.output (currentHead(gitCwd) / new Date().toISOString()), so no consumer is currently affected by the loss inside the embedded diagnostic string. This is a doc-completeness and silent-omission gap in the one path the module's own contract deliberately calls out for scrutiny, not a functional regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in commit 353eec69e1. The function doc promised nothing is discarded silently while describing only stages one through five, and the fallback record dropped two of the eight protected verdict fields without listing them - the single place in that function where something vanished unnamed. Stage six and the fallback are now documented, and the two fields are recorded properly rather than hardcoded: the protected set and the carryable set are two module constants, the dropped set is their difference intersected with the keys actually present, and the fallback record is built by iterating the constant instead of repeating its members, so the two lists cannot drift and protecting a field later without carrying it names it automatically. Verified: droppedKeys went from an empty array to timestamp and headSha, with the fallback path confirmed active and both fields confirmed absent from the record. That is the same move as the F-008 repair - make the property derived rather than remembered - which is the deepest lesson of this story and was applied here by the implementer unprompted.

findings.desc: Residual from F-006, not fully discharged by its own fix. .lattice/story/actives/B-3434/checklist.json still pins CHK-004:happy:0, CHK-004:edge:1 and CHK-004:adversarial:0 to the selector 'JSON contract intact', which is the tail of section 5's console.log at validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts:289 ('oversized realistic artifact is bounded with visible markers and JSON contract intact') -- a section that only proves CHK-004:edge:0's claim (visible truncation markers, no silent loss when outcome A is exercised). F-006's own resolvedReason said a new section was added that 'reads handlers/verifier.ts and asserts the disposition itself' so that 'a future silent un-wiring now fails a test instead of passing unnoticed', and recommended re-binding happy:0/edge:1/adversarial:0 to it. That section was genuinely added -- section 10 at validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts:565-597, console.log at line 596 ('CHK-004 disposition observed: outcome A (bound ships) is wired into persistStoryValidationEvidence, outcome B absent') -- and I independently confirmed by reading handlers/verifier.ts:842-861 that persistStoryValidationEvidence genuinely calls boundValidationEvidenceOutput and formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory and serialises boundedOutput.output, and that docs/requirements/decisions/validation-evidence-artifact-growth.md does not exist, so outcome A is truly wired and outcome B is truly absent today. But the checklist pins for happy:0/edge:1/adversarial:0 were never moved off 'JSON contract intact' onto section 10's line. Consequence: today's command exit code still gates correctly (one script, one process, any assertion failure anywhere fails the whole bound command), but the pin's own discriminating power -- the thing F-006 was filed to restore, per its own text 'a future refactor that silently un-wires those two calls... would sail through every CHK-004 selector unnoticed' -- is not restored. If a future edit DELETES section 10 outright (rather than making one of its assertions fail), section 5 still prints 'JSON contract intact' unchanged, selectorMatched stays true for all three intentRefs, and the governance proof F-006 fought for is gone with nothing to catch it. This is a live gap in the current tree, confirmed directly against checklist.json (not a stale read), not a hypothetical from an earlier round. Recommend re-binding happy:0/edge:1/adversarial:0 to the section-10 sentence in a follow-up edit.
findings.resolvedReason: Not repaired in the pins, and recorded here rather than closed silently, which is exactly what the reviewer who filed it asked for. Three CHK-004 intents remain pinned to a selector belonging to a section that does not discriminate their claim. The correct assertions now exist - the F-006 repair added a section that reads handlers/verifier.ts and asserts the disposition itself - but the pins were never moved from the old section to the new one, and they cannot be: a pin is immutable once bound and there is no sanctioned amend path. Neither existing escape applies. Restore-verbatim is meaningless because the old section still prints its line unchanged, and a waiver would understate evidence that genuinely exists. What is true today was verified independently rather than taken from the test's self-report: persistStoryValidationEvidence does call boundValidationEvidenceOutput and formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory and does serialise the bounded output, and the outcome-B rationale document does not exist. What remains exposed is narrower than a live coverage hole: if a future edit DELETES the new section outright rather than making one of its assertions fail, the old section still prints its line and all three refs stay matched with nothing to catch the loss. The reviewer's direct judgement, which I accept and am not softening for convenience, was that this should not gate DONE provided it is resolved on the record rather than dropped, because the substance is proven, the exit-code gate still catches a failing regression today, and the structural remedy - a pre-commit drift check plus an audited amend path - is filed as its own cross-story work citing three stories and three distinct stranding mechanisms. This is that record.

findings.desc: [codex host-B J1] Verified by main agent with an independent construction. The reducer measures the INNER JSON.stringify(result) string, but StoryStore places that string into TestEvidenceData.output and stringifies again, escaping it a second time; the 25 percent headroom cannot bound that expansion. My reproduction with 400 commands each carrying 12000 quote characters, duplicated into details as the producer does: inner output 19217147 bytes with withinBound true and reduced false - the reducer never engages - while the persisted file is 38422033 bytes, above the 33554432 read ceiling. So the refusal does not fire, the oversized file IS written, the immutable commit then hits the blob ceiling, the transaction rolls back, and that validation configuration can never persist evidence. The reuse path bypasses the reducer entirely via reusedStoryValidationResult. This is the story's own defect one layer out: measuring one thing and asserting it about another, which is the same shape as F-010. Fix by measuring the fully serialised TestEvidenceData at the writer boundary, escaping and outer fields included, and applying the bounded fallback there, reuse path included.

[codex host-B J2] Verified by main agent. Every successful return derives withinBound from the real encoding, so the flag is truthful - that part is sound. But the function is not TOTAL, contrary to the comment saying the last-resort replacement cannot fail and the smoke heading saying degenerate inputs never crash. JSON.stringify throws on cycles and BigInt; getters and proxies can throw during stringify, spread, Object.keys or the fallback scalar reads; a stateful getter that returned a large array twice and threw on the third read reached verdictOnlyRecord and threw there. An oversized primitive returns the oversized serialisation rather than a bounded replacement. Current callers construct plain JSON-shaped objects so no canonical gate path reaches these today, but the export takes unknown and the story's own stated rationale is that current-caller assumptions are insufficient.

[codex host-B J3] Verified by main agent. commitImmutableMetadataTree composes 'verified metadata is absent from the worktree: ' plus a joined path list without capDiagnostic, while verifyMetadataBlobDigests caps its equivalent. An exported arbitrary paths set can reach it when a hook, test seam or concurrent process removes files after isolated staging. Canonical callers use a tiny fixed set so this is not a present wedge, but it violates the exact rationale given for adding the aggregate cap in the first place - that a small path set is a property of current callers, not of an exported function.

[codex host-B J4] Verified by main agent. Maintenance assessment: relative to main the five files add 759 production and 1150 test lines, with complexity concentrated in a six-stage generic reducer while the real safety boundary is the final StoryStore serialisation. Stale or inaccurate claims remaining: that the returned output is always below the bound, that the last-resort replacement cannot fail, that test-evidence.json has an aggregate bound, and that the advisory leaves the verdict unchanged even on the refusal path. The smoke also claims no filesystem and pure functions while reading verifier source with readFileSync and existsSync. Suggested direction: a typed canonical validation result, one input-independent bounded fallback, and a postcondition over the complete persisted file. The metadata read and failure taxonomy is clear and does not need simplification.

F-015 is NOT fixed by e1afeb346a despite the commit message ("make the reducer total") and the new doc comment at validation-executor.ts:608-609 ("Total by construction... yields the bounded fallback or a refusal rather than an exception"). boundPersistedValidationEvidence (lines 611-677) still throws uncaught for a throwing getter/proxy on one of the six VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_VERDICT_ONLY_RECORD_KEYS. Root cause: the fallback call at line 666, `args.buildRecord(verdictOnlyRecord(args.result, measuredBytes))`, sits OUTSIDE the try block that ends at line 664 - unlike the two earlier buildRecord calls (642, 655) which are inside it. verdictOnlyRecord (517-537) reads `record[key]` directly for provider/status/allPass/allPassed/failureKind/summary with no try/catch of its own, so a getter that throws when accessed propagates straight out of boundPersistedValidationEvidence. Reproduced against the shipped dist build (node dist/core/validation-executor.js) with a minimal fixture: `{provider:"p",status:"pass",allPass:true,commands:[],details:[],warnings:[], get summary(){throw new Error("summary getter always throws")}}` passed to boundPersistedValidationEvidence({result, buildRecord}) throws uncaught, stack: `at get summary ... at verdictOnlyRecord (validation-executor.js:415:36) at boundPersistedValidationEvidence (validation-executor.js:528:45)`. The existing smoke (section 9, validation-evidence-buffer-smoke.ts) does not catch this because its throwing-getter fixture only throws on the 3rd+ read and the fixture is small enough that the FIRST reduction attempt succeeds without ever reaching the fallback branch at line 666, so PASS there does not exercise this call site. By contrast, positive verification: F-014 IS fixed - drove the real StoryStore.writeTestEvidence (not the measurement helper) against a scratch project root with a quote-heavy 1100-command fixture (20,594,242-byte inner JSON): bound.fileBytes (22,631,408) matched the real on-disk file size exactly, stayed under the 25,165,824-byte bound and 33,554,432-byte ceiling; the reuse path (reusedStoryValidationResult in verifier.ts) is also now wired through boundPersistedValidationEvidence. Recommendation: wrap the line-666 fallback build+measure (and the args.buildRecord(...) call itself, since a throwing buildRecord closure hits the same gap) in the same try/catch as the staged-reduction attempt, falling through to the refused disposition already used for the fileBytes===null case, rather than letting the exception escape the function.

Same defect as F-001/F-008/F-011, recurring a fourth and fifth time, and this commit did not touch either location (grep -n GUARANTEED\|guaranteed on the diff: zero hits).

LOCATION 1 (lines 139-160, the "What is guaranteed, and what is not" block, F-011's own paragraph). Its first bullet: "GUARANTEED for an input the reduction can act on - an object, which is what the only production caller passes: boundValidationEvidenceOutput returns a string strictly smaller than VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES." This commit removed stages 5 and 6 (drop-largest-field, truncate-in-place) from boundValidationEvidenceOutput and added its own adjacent comment saying the opposite: "There is deliberately no stage that makes this string total for arbitrary input. That guarantee belongs to boundPersistedValidationEvidence" (line ~486). Reproduced directly against the compiled function (tsc build of HEAD e1afeb346a to a scratch outDir, not the story's dist): calling boundValidationEvidenceOutput({allPass:true,...,someFieldAddedLater:'z'.repeat(30*MIB)}) - the exact "unknown field" fixture the smoke test uses, but through boundPersistedValidationEvidence rather than the reducer directly - returns outputWithinBound:false and an actual output of 31,457,588 bytes, nowhere near VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES (25,165,824). The "only production caller" clause is also now false: neither production call site (persistStoryValidationEvidence, reusedStoryValidationResult) calls boundValidationEvidenceOutput directly any more; both go through boundPersistedValidationEvidence, which is exactly what the removed guarantee moved to. The third bullet, "NOT GUARANTEED: that test-evidence.json as a FILE is under the ceiling," is now backwards for the same reason: making that true (with a refusal fallback when it can't be) is this commit's entire purpose.

LOCATION 2 (lines 237-240), the function-level docstring on formatValidationEvidenceAdvisory: "Deliberately worded as information: no failure vocabulary, ... and an explicit statement that the validate verdict is untouched, so a reader scanning output cannot mistake it for a failing check." Four lines below, this commit's OWN new inline comment says the opposite: "The wording deliberately avoids every failure token, ... cannot mistake this line for a check that did not pass - EXCEPT on the refusal path, where the write genuinely does not happen and saying otherwise would be the inaccuracy" (line ~245), and the refused branch's actual text opens "evidence size limit reached" with no "verdict is unchanged" claim - the smoke test itself asserts `doesNotMatch(advisory, /verdict is unchanged/)` on that path (section 10). The refusal-path exception was correctly implemented in the function body by this same commit; the docstring immediately above it was not revisited to state the exception, so it now blanket-asserts the one thing the function's newest branch was written specifically to NOT do.

Both are the shape the story exists to remove: a paragraph true of an old owner/old behaviour, left standing after the commit that changed the owner/behaviour, with the correction sitting a few lines below where nobody reads it against the paragraph above.

Task question: "does verdict_only ever get returned for input that was NOT degenerate, and is the reader told the difference between 'reduced successfully' and 'replaced because it could not be reduced'?" Answer to both: yes it fires on non-degenerate input, and no, disposition carries no information distinguishing the two causes.

Root cause: boundPersistedValidationEvidence's escaping-expansion correction is a SINGLE-SHOT heuristic, not a loop. Its own docstring (line ~599) enumerates exactly THREE steps: (1) reduce once and measure the file, (2) if that doesn't fit, replace with verdictOnlyRecord and measure, (3) if that still doesn't fit, refuse. The actual code has FOUR: between (1) and (2) there is an undocumented retry - compute an "expansion" ratio from the one measurement already taken, derive a smaller innerBudget, re-run boundValidationEvidenceOutput ONCE more at that budget, and if THAT single retry doesn't land under the bound, fall straight to verdictOnlyRecord. There is no iteration toward convergence and no second retry with a further-adjusted budget - a reader of the docstring would not know this step exists at all, let alone that it can fail.

Reproduced: constructed a `details` array (96,000 entries total) with two populations of different escaping density - 16,000 pure-quote entries (each character doubles on the second stringify) placed first, and 80,000 plain 'a' entries placed after, so the array-end-popping reduction (stage 2) removes the low-density population first and the high-density population survives longest. At the reducer's default budget the first pass legitimately reduces to inner.serializedBytes=25,165,752 (just under the 25,165,824-byte inner bound), with 34,125 real detail lines surviving - genuinely reducible content, correctly reduced. boundPersistedValidationEvidence then measures the file, finds it over, computes an expansion ratio from a remainder whose average density does not match what the smaller retry budget will actually leave behind (the surviving low-density population gets consumed faster than the ratio assumes), retries ONCE at the derived innerBudget, and that retry still lands over the file bound. Result: disposition="verdict_only", fileBytes=541, and every one of the 34,125 legitimately-reduced detail lines is thrown away in favour of a bare verdict stub - identical in shape and in `disposition` value to the truly-degenerate cases (bulk in an unknown field, a 30MB key name, a 30MB verdict scalar) that the smoke test's section 8 uses to justify the SAME label. allPass/status do survive (verified: parsed output.allPass===true, status==="pass"), so the phase-gate contract holds, but every readable per-command result is gone for an input that had 34,125 lines of real, already-correctly-reduced evidence one budget-adjustment away from fitting.

This is not a hypothetical shape: validate.commands mixing JSON-emitting tools (quote-heavy output) with plain-text tools (log-heavy output) across 100+ configured commands is an ordinary repository shape, not a constructed edge case.

Fix direction: either loop the retry (recompute innerBudget from the retry's own measured expansion, bounded iteration count) until convergence or a real ceiling is hit, or report a disposition value that distinguishes "the heuristic did not converge" from "there is genuinely nothing left to reduce" so a reader - and a future maintainer deciding whether to improve the heuristic - is not told the two are the same event.

Repro environment note: verified against a `tsc -p packages/main/tsconfig.json` build of HEAD e1afeb346a to a private scratch outDir (worktree dist was not modified), using boundValidationEvidenceOutput/boundPersistedValidationEvidence/measurePersistedEvidenceBytes/VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_BOUND_BYTES imported directly; happy to hand over the exact repro script on request.

In reusedStoryValidationResult, the new F-014 bound check does: `if (!reusedBound.withinBound) { throw new Error(...) }`. Every other "cannot proceed" branch in this same function - missing prior commandExecution, preexisting dirty managed metadata - returns `externalResult({ provider: 'lattice-verifier-reuse-persistence', status: 'fail', failureKind: 'infra_failure', ... })`, a structured, catchable result the rest of the pipeline (decorateAndMaybePersistStoryValidation, renderExternalResult, --json output) knows how to render. The parallel executed-path equivalent in persistStoryValidationEvidence (the function this commit is otherwise symmetric with) also returns a structured value: `return persistenceFailure(...)`, not a throw.

Mechanically this is not a lock leak - withValidationExecutionLock releases via try/finally regardless of how fn() exits - so it is not a correctness blocker. But it means the identical condition (evidence file cannot be reduced under the bound; refuse the write) surfaces two different ways depending only on which of the two near-duplicate code paths hit it: a clean "Validation FAIL: <reason>" result on the executed path, and an uncaught exception on the reuse path, which - absent a catch somewhere further up the CLI/handler chain that the story did not add and that lives outside allowedModify (cli-engine.ts is explicitly excluded from this story's scope) - most likely renders as a raw stack trace rather than the operator-facing message the identical executed-path condition produces.

Suggested fix: mirror persistenceFailure's shape (or literally reuse it) in reusedStoryValidationResult rather than throwing, so the two paths this commit made symmetric for the bounding logic are also symmetric for the resulting failure surface.

packages/main/src/core/validation-executor.ts:517-537,611-677 (boundPersistedValidationEvidence / verdictOnlyRecord): the pre-fix smoke (e1afeb346a~1, section 8e) asserted that an irreducible input honestly reports withinBound=false ("an unmet bound is refused... never flagged as success", matching CHK-004:adversarial:1). The rewritten smoke drops that assertion entirely -- no fixture calls persist()/boundPersistedValidationEvidence with a non-object `result` -- and section 9 (degenerate inputs) only covers cyclic/BigInt/throwing-getter, all of which are objects. I confirmed by executing packages/main/dist/core/validation-executor.js directly (not via the committed smoke) that the property actually flipped: boundPersistedValidationEvidence({result: "x".repeat(30*1024*1024), buildRecord}) now returns disposition=verdict_only, withinBound=true, fileBytes=507, with a persisted output of `{"evidenceBound":{...}}` carrying NEITHER allPass NOR status (verdictOnlyRecord:518 treats any non-object source as `{}`, so none of VALIDATION_EVIDENCE_VERDICT_ONLY_RECORD_KEYS survive). Same result for `result: undefined`. This is the opposite of the old honest-refusal guarantee and is not covered by any committed test, so a future change that makes this path reachable (result is typed `any` at the two production call sites in handlers/verifier.ts) would silently report success while persisting evidence with no verdict at all -- exactly the failure mode CHK-004 exists to prevent. WHY: this is a real behavior change (verified by direct execution against the built dist, not speculation) in a class of input the story previously tested and guaranteed honestly-refuses; it is currently reachable only defensively (both current call sites always pass well-formed ValidationResult objects), so it is not release-blocking, but it is untested in either direction and should get either a committed assertion pinning the current (silent-success) behavior as intentional, or a fix routing non-object/unserialisable-verdict inputs to the refused disposition the way the old code did.

Re-filed under the quality lane so it actually gates (story B-3434:F-014, agent=main/RR-011, is not reviewer evidence per core/review-run.ts isReviewerAgent). Independently re-verified against the pre-fix tree (before commit e1afeb346a) by reading the write path myself: boundValidationEvidenceOutput's postcondition (withinBound derived from Buffer.byteLength of the string it RETURNS) was enforced at the wrong boundary. handlers/verifier.ts persistStoryValidationEvidence assigned that already-bounded string to TestEvidenceData.output, a single string field, then StoryStore.writeJsonFile (core/store.ts) ran JSON.stringify(data, null, 2) on the OUTER object a second time, re-escaping every quote/backslash already present in the inner JSON string. I reproduced this myself on the pre-fix build with 400 commands x 12000 quote-heavy chars each, duplicated into details as the producer does: inner output ~19.2MB with withinBound true, while the persisted file measured 38,422,033 bytes, above the 33,554,432-byte read ceiling -- the exact incident this story exists to prevent, recreated one call frame further out. The reuse path (reusedStoryValidationResult) bypassed the reducer entirely via output: JSON.stringify(reused), with no bound at all. THIS IS NOW FIXED as of commit e1afeb346a, which I independently verified on the current tree (HEAD e1afeb346a): boundPersistedValidationEvidence({result, buildRecord}) now measures Buffer.byteLength(JSON.stringify(record,null,2)+"\n") -- the exact bytes StoryStore.writeJsonFile writes -- on the FULLY BUILT record, and I confirmed this matches an actual on-disk file byte-for-byte in a live write test (22,555,544 bytes measured == 22,555,544 bytes on disk). The reuse path now calls the same boundPersistedValidationEvidence and checks .withinBound before writing (verifier.ts reusedStoryValidationResult, lines ~721-745). Filing as resolved; resolving in the next call with the verification detail.
